In situations involving alleged physical and verbal abuse, the absolute priority must be safety. Generally, mental health professionals strongly advise against couples counseling or joint sessions when intimate partner violence is present. Even if the client is amenable to the idea, joint sessions can be highly dangerous. An abusive partner may use what is shared during a session to further manipulate, control, or physically retaliate against the victim behind closed doors. Because of this, individual support focused on safety planning and empowerment is the standard recommendation, rather than joint relationship repair.

If you or someone you know is navigating domestic abuse, please consider reaching out to a dedicated support service. In the United States, the National Domestic Violence Hotline is available 24/7 by calling 1-800-799-SAFE (7233) or texting "START" to 88788. They can provide confidential guidance on safely navigating these complex and dangerous dynamics.
